beats.text: Heartbleed was a missing length check, not a cracked cipher.
beats.note: The researchers called it a programming mistake in OpenSSL, not a flaw in the protocol.

beats.name: Robin Seggelmann
beats.role: Wrote the heartbeat feature and later said he missed validating a variable containing a length. A reviewer missed it too, and it was committed on 31 December 2011.

beats.context: How much of a server's memory one malformed heartbeat request could read back. An attacker could simply ask again.

beats.lead: It sat there for over two years
beats.text: The flawed code shipped by default in March 2012 and was disclosed in April 2014.
beats.note: About 17% of trusted secure web servers were thought to be vulnerable.

beats.text: Google's Neel Mehta and the security firm Codenomicon found it independently.
beats.note: Mehta reported it to OpenSSL on 1 April 2014. The fix, version 1.0.1g, came on 7 April.

beats.line: One missing check. Half a million servers.
